questions: is nvda r&d spend high compared to peers
sales lowish this quarter for nike?
is XYZ's cash low for its size
entries.market_reading: A claim that a figure sits below or above a reference level. The market always means 'low or high compared with something' - the company's own recent history, its industry peers, its size, or what the figure has to cover - and never low or high on its own.
entries.formula: Resolve the concept named (another family's entry supplies the figure), compute it, then place it in one or more stated frames: its percentile or distance from the median within the company's own history window; its percentile within a stated peer set; its ratio to a size base (revenue, total assets, market value); its ratio to the obligation it must cover; or its position against an authority-drawn line where one exists (see QF-23).
entries.period_convention: Latest comparable level (TTM or latest fiscal year for flows; latest balance-sheet date for balances) against the same measure over the history window (commonly the last 3-5 fiscal years, or the same fiscal quarter across years for seasonal businesses).
entries.frame_notes: history: 'low' = below the company's own median or range over a stated window. peers: below the median (or in the lower quartile) of a stated peer set with the same period basis. scale: small relative to revenue, assets or market value (common-size). obligations: does not cover what it must pay (coverage < 1). absolute: below a line fixed by an authority (few exist: bank capital categories, SEC filer-size tests, going-concern horizon). When the user gives no frame, a careful analyst states the level, shows it against the company's own history and, where a peer set exists, peers, names both frames, and draws no adjective the frames do not support.
entries.direction: depends on the concept: higher is better for margins, cash flow and coverage; lower is better for leverage, costs and days receivable; for inventory, cash holdings and payout both extremes can be read as bad

thresholds.line: value < 0
thresholds.meaning: a negative figure (loss, outflow, negative equity) is a different state, stated as such, not a degree of 'low'

thresholds.line: coverage < 1.0
thresholds.meaning: the resource does not cover the obligation it is compared with

questions: did nvidia have a strong quarter
entries.market_reading: For results, 'weak' or 'strong' usually means versus the same quarter a year earlier and versus what the market expected; for a balance sheet it means capacity to absorb shocks - liquidity and leverage relative to obligations and peers.
entries.formula: Results: year-over-year change (and its sign) of the headline measures for the same fiscal quarter or TTM - revenue, operating income, diluted EPS, operating cash flow. Balance sheet: net debt = total debt minus cash and short-term investments, plus leverage and coverage placed in the history and peer frames.
entries.period_convention: YoY same fiscal quarter (or TTM vs TTM a year earlier) for results; latest balance-sheet date for the balance sheet; TTM flows for coverage.
entries.frame_notes: The commonest market reading of a 'weak quarter' is versus consensus estimates or company guidance. Consensus is private data; guidance sits in press releases (8-K exhibits), usually non-GAAP and unaudited. From filings alone the product can only say weak or strong versus the company's own prior periods and versus peers. 'Strong balance sheet' commonly means net cash (cash and short-term investments exceed debt), low leverage against peers, and ample coverage of the next 12 months' obligations.
entries.direction: higher is better for results; more net cash and less leverage is stronger

thresholds.line: net debt < 0 (cash and short-term investments exceed total debt)
thresholds.meaning: net cash position; a definitional basis often used for 'strong balance sheet', not an authority-drawn line

questions: is boeing in good shape financially
how healthy is ford's balance sheet
entries.market_reading: A composite judgement across liquidity (can it pay what falls due), leverage and solvency (can it carry its debt), profitability and cash generation. The market reads it dimension by dimension, not as one number.
entries.formula: Report each dimension separately and frame each: liquidity (current ratio, cash ratio, cash vs 12-month obligations), leverage (debt to equity, debt to EBITDA), coverage (operating income or EBITDA to interest expense), profitability (margins, return on assets), cash generation (operating and free cash flow). For banks use regulatory capital ratios instead of the current ratio.
entries.period_convention: Latest balance sheet for balances; TTM or latest fiscal year for flows; 3-5 years for trend.
entries.frame_notes: history and peers for every dimension; obligations for liquidity and coverage; absolute only for regulated entities (bank prompt-corrective-action categories) and for the binary going-concern disclosure. Census QFR publishes exactly these dimensions for covered industries: current ratio, cash and securities to current liabilities, equity to total debt, annualized profit rates.

thresholds.line: (A)-(D): total risk-based capital >= 10.0%, tier 1 >= 8.0%, CET1 >= 6.5%, leverage >= 5.0% (12 CFR 324.403(b)(1)(i)); a qualifying community banking organization that has elected the community bank leverage ratio framework (324.12) is deemed to meet (A)-(D) (324.403(b)(1)(ii)); AND (E): the institution is not subject to any written agreement, order, capital directive or prompt corrective action directive to meet and maintain a specific capital level
thresholds.meaning: 'well capitalized': the FDIC's prompt-corrective-action category, drawn for purposes of section 38 of the FDI Act, for FDIC-supervised insured institutions (bank level, not the holding company that files the 10-K); the FDIC's line for its own purpose, not a market line for 'healthy' or 'safe'. (E) is not computable from ratios alone. A CBLR bank's risk-based ratios may go unreported: that reads 'cannot establish', never 'not well capitalized'

thresholds.line: substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern is stated in the filing and NOT alleviated by management's plans (ASC 205-40-50-13, by reference)
thresholds.meaning: read, not computed: management's statement (us-gaap:SubstantialDoubtAboutGoingConcernWithinOneYear = true, which FASB references to ASC 205-40-50-13 and 50-14) or the auditor's explanatory paragraph under PCAOB AS 2415. FASB's test, applied by management, and PCAOB's, applied by the auditor. Doubt alleviated by management's plans (ASC 205-40-50-12, by reference; tagged separately as SubstantialDoubtAboutGoingConcernManagementsPlansSubstantialDoubtAlleviated) is not this line, and an absent tag or paragraph is not a finding: it reads 'cannot establish'

entries.frame_notes: The Federal Reserve reads corporate leverage as high relative to its historical distribution and pairs it with interest coverage - the history and obligations frames used by a public authority. entries.market_reading: The direction of change of a measure across consecutive comparable periods, judged in the direction that is better for that measure (margin up = improving; days sales outstanding up = deteriorating). One change is a change; a trend needs several comparable periods.
entries.formula: Compute the measure for consecutive comparable periods (fiscal years; same fiscal quarter year-over-year; or TTM rolled each quarter); report the sign of each change, how many consecutive moves share a direction, and the latest change against the company's typical period-to-period movement.
entries.period_convention: YoY same quarter or TTM rolling; at least three comparable points to call a trend.
entries.frame_notes: Direction is judged against the company's own past; peers can add 'improving faster than peers'. MD&A (Item 303) carries management's discussion of known trends - quote it as the company's statement, not as a finding.
entries.direction: depends on the measure (use the measure's own better-direction)

entries.period_convention: YoY for the latest period; 3- or 5-year CAGR for multi-year growth.

entries.market_reading: Whether a payout, growth rate or margin can continue from the company's own internally generated resources without rising borrowing or asset sales. 'Sustainable' is also used for ESG and climate topics - a different question the product must disambiguate.

figures.name: dividends paid
figures.notes: 10-Q values are YTD. Primary: PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock (common dividends of the parent), matching the parent-level NetIncomeLoss denominator. Fallback PaymentsOfDividends includes distributions to preferred shareholders and noncontrolling interests, and is labelled so when used. On a declared basis: CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared / diluted EPS.

figures.name: net income
figures.notes: Fallback us-gaap:ProfitLoss only when the period reports no noncontrolling interest: ProfitLoss includes the NCI share, and the payout ratio is on earnings attributable to the parent.

figures.name: dividends declared per share
figures.notes: declared, not paid

entries.formula: payout ratio = common dividends paid (PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock) / net income attributable to the parent (NetIncomeLoss), or on a declared basis CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared / diluted EPS; cash payout = (dividends [+ buybacks]) / free cash flow; above 100% the distribution exceeds what the period earned or generated. Sustainable growth rate = ROE x retention ratio (1 - payout), a textbook definition.
entries.period_convention: TTM or latest fiscal year; several years for persistence.
entries.frame_notes: obligations: are distributions covered by earnings and free cash flow; history: is coverage falling; peers: payout norms differ widely by industry (REITs and MLPs are judged on FFO or distributable cash flow, other families).
entries.direction: lower payout and higher coverage is more sustainable

thresholds.line: payout ratio > 100% of net income or of free cash flow
thresholds.meaning: the company distributed more than it earned or generated in the period; definitional arithmetic, not a prediction of a cut

entries.market_reading: A quantity judged against what supports it: debt against earnings, cash flow, equity or covenant limits; spending against revenue and peers; inventory against sales; share issuance against the existing count (dilution).

figures.name: total debt
figures.notes: Primary: LongTermDebt + ShortTermBorrowings. Use CommercialPaper (and the other short-term components) only when ShortTermBorrowings is not reported: in FASB's calculation CommercialPaper is a component of ShortTermBorrowings, so adding both counts it twice. Fallbacks, in order: (1) DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount where the filer tags it; (2) LongTermDebtNoncurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent + ShortTermBorrowings; (3) LongTermDebtNoncurrent + DebtCurrent, where DebtCurrent stands in for (LongTermDebtCurrent + ShortTermBorrowings) and is labelled as including current finance lease liabilities. Never pair DebtCurrent with LongTermDebt. LongTermDebt includes current maturities (its noncurrent sibling is labelled 'Excluding Current Maturities'); never add DebtCurrent or LongTermDebtCurrent to it. Excludes lease obligations unless DebtCurrent is used, and says so when it is.

figures.name: diluted weighted-average shares
figures.notes: for dilution trend; not additive across periods

entries.formula: ratio of the quantity to its capacity base (debt / EBITDA, debt / equity, interest / operating income; R&D or capex as % of revenue; inventory days; year-over-year % change in diluted shares), placed in history and peer frames and against any contractual limit the company discloses.
entries.period_convention: Latest balance sheet for balances; TTM for flow denominators.
entries.frame_notes: No universal debt line exists. Covenant maxima are company-specific lines in debt notes and filed credit agreements. Rating-agency methodology maps leverage ratios to named bands (tier 2, by reference only). Census QFR publishes equity to total debt for covered industries. The Federal Reserve judges leverage against its historical distribution alongside interest coverage.
entries.direction: lower is better for debt and dilution; spending depends on strategy

questions: does XYZ have enough money to last the year
is there enough liquidity at this bank
enough cash to pay the notes due next year?
entries.market_reading: Whether resources on hand, plus what the business generates, cover what falls due over a stated horizon - usually the next twelve months - read as a coverage ratio where 1.0 means exactly covered.

figures.name: debt maturing within one year
figures.notes: Long-term debt due: LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextRollingTwelveMonths, else LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths (label 'Year One': the next fiscal year, so a 12-month figure only at a fiscal year-end), else LongTermDebtCurrent. Add ShortTermBorrowings, and CommercialPaper only when it is tagged separately and not already inside a reported ShortTermBorrowings (in FASB's calculation it is a component of it). DebtCurrent is an alternative total (short-term borrowings + current long-term debt + current finance lease liabilities): never added to the others, and labelled as including leases when used. The maturity table is usually in the 10-K only.

figures.name: current assets / current liabilities
figures.notes: not presented by banks and most insurers

entries.formula: (cash and equivalents + current short-term investments, at the balance-sheet date) / (debt due within 12 months at the same date: LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextRollingTwelveMonths, else LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths at a fiscal year-end only, else LongTermDebtCurrent, plus ShortTermBorrowings, and CommercialPaper only where tagged separately from ShortTermBorrowings; DebtCurrent only when those are not separately tagged). Show N1 (cash and equivalents alone) and N2 (plus short-term investments) and name the one used. Show undrawn committed credit (LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity, often untagged text) beside the ratio as a separately described source, and never add it to the numerator. Add no operating cash flow, projected or trailing, and no forecast obligations. S&P's 'adequate' liquidity test (forecast sources / uses >= 1.2x over 12 months, among other tests) is S&P's line, drawn on S&P's forecasts, and is never computed or shown. thresholds.line: SEC Rule 12b-2. LAF: public float >= $700m. AF: float $75m to < $700m. Each applies ONLY if the issuer has been reporting for at least 12 months, has filed at least one annual report, and is NOT SRC-eligible under the revenue test (so a $75m-$700m float with revenue < $100m is a non-accelerated filer). Status is set at fiscal year-end, using float as of the last business day of Q2. Exit: a LAF leaves at float < $560m (it becomes an AF if float is $60m to < $560m) or on revenue-test SRC eligibility. An AF leaves at float < $60m or on revenue-test SRC eligibility. SRC entry: float < $250m, or revenue < $100m with either no float or float < $700m. Lower re-qualification lines apply after an issuer loses SRC status (e.g. float < $200m). EGC: revenue < $1,235,000,000 in the latest fiscal year is the entry test only; status ends at the earliest of the fiscal year-end in which revenue reaches that amount, the fiscal year-end after the fifth anniversary of the first registered sale of common equity, more than $1bn of non-convertible debt issued in the previous three years, or becoming a LAF

entries.market_reading: The same fact (concept, period, dimensions, unit) is reported again in later filings - as comparatives, recasts (discontinued operations, segment changes, new accounting principles) or error corrections - and the value can change. Two answers are legitimate: the latest value filed, and the value known at a given date; a careful product states which.

A 10-K/A replaces only the items it contains.

entries.market_reading: An honest statement that the product could not compute the figure or could not apply a frame, with the reason - never a finding that the figure is zero, low, declining or bad.
entries.formula: Return 'could not establish' with one reason: (1) company unresolved or ambiguous (QF-46/47); (2) figure not tagged under any element in the fallback list - list the elements tried; absence is not zero; (3) nil tagged, which is not zero; (4) period not filed yet, or a derivation input missing (Q4 needs FY and nine months); (5) quantity not derivable by subtraction (EPS, weighted shares, instants, ratios); (6) denominator zero or negative - ratio not meaningful; (7) frame unavailable - fewer comparable history points or peers than the stated minimum, or Census QFR does not cover the industry; (8) needs data outside filings (prices, consensus, forecasts, private data); (9) conflicting values the as-of rule cannot order; (10) stale - the latest filing is older than expected (late filer, NT notice): answer with the latest period and say it is stale; (11) no authoritative line - report the value in its frames and say no line exists, instead of refusing.
entries.period_convention: State the period and the filing date that the answer (or the refusal) refers to.
entries.frame_notes: Applies to every frame: a missing frame is reported as missing, never replaced by an unstated one.

notes: 1) Every qualifier here is comparative: 'low', 'high', 'weak', 'cheap', 'too much' mean 'relative to a frame' - own history, peers, size, or the obligation to be covered - and an authority draws a line only in narrow scopes (bank capital categories, SEC filer-size tests, the one-year going-concern and 12-month liquidity horizons) or by arithmetic (0, 1.0, 100%). A product must name the frame it used; with no frame available it reports the value and says 'could not establish' for the adjective (QF-48 reason 11). 2) The frames need clean periods: 10-Q cash flows are year-to-date only (Reg S-X 10-01(c)(3)); the 10-K no longer carries quarterly data (Item 302 since 10 Feb 2021), so quarterly cash flow and Q4 are derived by subtraction, and never for instants, EPS, weighted shares or ratios. 3) Select facts by (concept, period dates, dimensions, unit) and filing date under the as-of rule, never by concept name alone. 4) Peer benchmarks differ in construction: Census QFR is public domain but domestic-only, a ratio of aggregate totals, NAICS-based and limited to mining, manufacturing, trade and selected services; EDGAR carries SEC-assigned SIC codes; GICS is proprietary and unusable. 5) Element names drift across taxonomy years (e.g. SalesRevenueNet, TreasuryStockShares and CashAndCashEquivalentsPeriodIncreaseDecrease are absent from the 2026 taxonomy); keep ordered fallbacks and record which element supplied each value. 6) Rules of thumb from practitioners are labelled as such and never presented as authority lines; the SEC staff's own statement (SAB 99) is that no numerical threshold alone settles significance. 7) Several entries (QF-26 to QF-45) are mechanics, not qualifiers; their thresholds are empty by construction. 8) Every public-domain quote in this file was re-read on its page with siglia-def-check at 2026-09-24T05:15-05:16Z (eCFR as of 2026-09-22, govinfo Federal Register HTML, census.gov, federalreserve.gov) and found; the two Census PDF quotes (S23, S24) were read from the PDFs with pypdf at 05:0xZ, since that tool does not parse PDFs.
